title: Universal Robots UR5e - ROS 2 Jazzy

moveit.title: MoveIt 2 with mock hardware (start the mock driver first)
moveit.cmd: ros2 launch ur_robot_driver ur_control.launch.py ur_type:=ur5e robot_ip:=yyy.yyy.yyy.yyy use_mock_hardware:=true launch_rviz:=false
moveit.then: ros2 launch ur_moveit_config ur_moveit.launch.py ur_type:=ur5e launch_rviz:=true

example.title: Example trajectory (with the Gazebo sim running)

real.title: Real UR5e (ur_robot_driver)
real.cmd: ros2 launch ur_robot_driver ur_control.launch.py ur_type:=ur5e robot_ip:=192.168.56.101 launch_rviz:=true
real.then: ros2 launch ur_moveit_config ur_moveit.launch.py ur_type:=ur5e launch_rviz:=true
real.needs: a UR5e (PolyScope 5.x) with the External Control URCap installed
real.notes: Use the robot's IP address; install the externalcontrol URCap from ur_robot_driver/resources and start the program on the teach pendant. URSim works too: ros2 run ur_client_library start_ursim.sh -m ur5e
real.status_reason: Real-hardware entry of a course robot (behind the hardware license lock).

steps: sudo apt install python3-vcstool python3-colcon-common-extensions python3-rosdep

honesty: The site runs these real launch files, YAML, URDF/xacro and SDF files in the browser and models the programs they start (gz sim, controller_manager, move_group, Nav2 servers ...) in JavaScript. It cannot run the compiled C++ nodes. On a real Ubuntu 24.04 + ROS 2 Jazzy machine the same workspace builds and runs with the steps below.
pruned: Only the mesh/texture files used by the robots and worlds listed in 'gallery' and the entries are shipped (vcs import gets the complete repositories).
